purpose: Which paint mixture gives the largest contribution within the available material?
meaning: Intersect nonnegative production choices with the two fixed capacities and the total-material half-plane. Evaluate the linear contribution at every resulting vertex and retain all maximizing vertices. A shared optimal edge or a flat objective remains visible.

definition.setting: A paint workshop can make at most four litres of a first blend and three litres of a second. Both use one litre of base per litre made. The available base material moves one boundary of the feasible polygon. Contribution rates may be positive or negative, so leaving material unused can be best.

conditions: The quantities are continuous litres, not indivisible cans. The fixed capacities are four and three litres; total base ranges from zero to seven litres. Rates range from −3 to 5 credits per litre. The feasible set always contains the origin and is bounded. This two-variable family does not implement arbitrary constraints, integer programming, infeasibility or unboundedness.

properties.derivation: Every feasible point is a convex combination of the polygon vertices. Its linear contribution is the same combination of their contributions, so it cannot exceed the largest vertex contribution. Equal best endpoints make their whole edge optimal.
